title: Install alignment and active-Agent self-review through a native MCP Adapter

requirement.summary: Provide a lightweight foreground STDIO MCP Adapter that lets a current Coding Agent use the implemented alignment and medium-risk self-review state machines through model-controlled tools, with Codex as the first project-local installation proof and no user-authored protocol JSON or second-model setup.

objective.rationale: The foreground JSONL protocol is executable but ordinary Coding Agent surfaces do not own its records. A model-controlled MCP tool boundary is the smallest native host integration that can keep Core model-free, reuse current-agent entitlement, and remain portable beyond one vendor.

goal: Add a vendor-neutral foreground MCP Adapter over the existing alignment and active-Agent self-review state machines, expose a reviewed project-local Codex configuration, and prove the current Agent can complete the normalized journey without user-authored JSON, another account, or Core model calls.
non_goals: Do not add an OpenAI, Anthropic, or general model SDK; call a model from AgentGov; configure an API key; start a second Agent; or implement the independent high-risk Reviewer.
Do not treat Codex command hooks as model-capable prompt or agent handlers; current released hooks execute commands only.
Do not send raw prompts, raw answers, transcripts, assistant messages, full source content, credentials, model prompts, absolute paths, or host-selected governance identities into Core.

Do not let an MCP tool admit tasks, start development sessions, modify requirements or architecture, expand scope, approve exceptions, authorize code/Git/publication/release/deployment, or perform external writes.
Do not persist dialogue or self-review state across Adapter restart, write runtime/repository state from MCP tools, or run a background daemon.
Do not claim that offline protocol tests prove Codex, Claude Code, or an IDE will always select the right tool or perform correct semantic reasoning.
Do not change stable 0.2.1, immutable v0.3.0rc1, release metadata, workflows, consumer repositories, or external systems.
acceptance_signals: A dependency-free foreground STDIO JSON-RPC MCP server supports current discovery/tool calls plus the legacy initialize path needed for host compatibility, emits only protocol JSON on stdout, and sends diagnostics only to stderr.

The server advertises a deterministic minimal tool set for starting/updating/resolving alignment and starting/completing active-Agent self-review, with strict JSON Schemas, read-only/advisory annotations, and server instructions that keep the workflow in order.

Each journey returns an explicit opaque handle; every later call must present that handle and the exact pending prompt/request binding. Unknown, duplicate, stale, out-of-order, cross-journey, cross-Adapter, or restarted calls fail without advancing state.

Tools accept only normalized center/drift/question/resolution/observation drafts. The Adapter, not the model, generates contract IDs, digests, timestamps, route/Provider bindings, observation identities, result identity, privacy declarations, and denied authority.

Self-review starts only after the same journey has a human-owned resolved alignment, uses an available medium-risk active-host Provider supplied by the host Adapter, and completes only through the existing active-Agent result builder.
MCP calls make zero AgentGov model/network calls, write no repository/runtime state, survive no process restart, and cannot claim independent assurance or downstream authority.

A create-missing-only Codex project integration plan/config launches the packaged AgentGov MCP command, requires normal trusted-project/config review, and does not overwrite an existing .codex/config.toml or change the existing hook trust boundary.
Codex and Claude Code Provider fixtures exercise the same in-process MCP tool journey without vendor branches in Core; Codex-specific configuration remains in the Adapter integration layer.

Tests cover discovery, legacy initialization, tool listing/calls, JSON-RPC errors, complete alignment-to-review flow, invalid atomic retry, restart loss, privacy/authority rejection, CLI STDIO framing, config conflict/preserve/create behavior, and documentation truthfulness.

Affected source-of-truth and public documentation distinguish implemented MCP protocol/configuration from unproven native model tool selection, future Claude/IDE installation, and independent high-risk Reviewer work.
Focused/full tests, current-task, scope, repository, schemas, compile, and diff validation pass.

items: A model-controlled tool sequence could cross journey, prompt, Provider, or pending self-review bindings after retry or restart.
A host could forward raw conversation or source content into normalized tool arguments unless schemas and runtime validation fail closed.
Project-local MCP configuration is executable and therefore must retain Codex trusted-project/config review rather than being silently installed.
MCP and Codex capabilities are evolving; the implementation must state the tested protocol/configuration boundary and avoid claiming unsupported hook agent execution.

stop_conditions: Stop if the MCP Adapter needs raw/private content, model credentials, a Core model call, a second Agent, background persistence, or a repository/runtime write.
Stop if a model can provide governance identities, skip the resolved human alignment, cross journey/Adapter/request bindings, or gain project/external authority.
Stop if project configuration can overwrite existing .codex/config.toml, bypass Codex trust review, or claim automatic support in an untested host.
Stop if ordinary users must author JSON-RPC/tool payloads, repeatedly confirm medium-risk self-review, or configure a second model/account.
Stop before external network/model calls, Git writes, publication, release, deployment, or consumer mutation.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed the completed native MCP Adapter, accepted its purpose and benefits, and explicitly authorized the next development step on 2026-08-06. This task is paused for routing hygiene only; it does not claim publication, release, or consumer adoption.
